slides.headline: Consolidating three depots saves $4.1M a year at a one-time cost of $2.6M.
slides.answer: Consolidating three depots saves $4.1M a year — for a one-time cost of $2.6M and no loss of next-day coverage.
keyLines: Three depots run below 40% utilisation and sit within 60 miles of a larger site.
Their volume fits inside the receiving sites' spare capacity with 18% headroom.
Next-day coverage holds for 99.2% of current customers after re-routing.
The saving is dominated by lease and labour; fuel rises by $0.3M and is included.
slides.decision: Approve the consolidation plan and the $2.6M transition budget by Oct 15.
slides.risk: Union consultation at the Ridgeway depot could add four months.

slides.headline: Close three underused depots now, before the Oakmont lease renews at a 12% step-up.
slides.situation: Halvard runs nine depots sized for a network that had the Carver contract.
slides.complication: Carver ended; three depots have run below 40% utilisation for six quarters, and the Oakmont lease renews in March.
slides.resolution: Move their volume to Easton and Fairmont over nine months: $4.1M a year saved, next-day kept for 99.2% of customers.

rows.risk: Union consultation at Ridgeway extends beyond four months
rows.mitigation: Start informal engagement now; sequence Oakmont and Brookline first so savings begin regardless.

rows.risk: Easton peak-week capacity is tighter than modelled
rows.mitigation: Pilot a peak week in December before committing; Fairmont takes overflow.
